status: B9, 17 November 2026. Our side's radio intercept service for the enemy's air radio: its posts in the chain of command (chain_pannonia.json), their linguists, what they write wrong, and how fast what they read reaches the battery (simcore/command/intercept.hpp, docs/air_battle/09_COMMS_AND_INTERCEPT.md section 4 and 5).
source: osipov_2013 (a Soviet voice intercept operator, 1981-83: English learnt in civilian life, forms and tape, a doubtful translation checked the same day by telephone); nsa_purple_dragon_1993 pp. 60-61, 68-69 (the relay of intercepted traffic in about five minutes; a company of 130 processed 7,745 messages in a month); npic_1981_intercept; bischoff_fufutakl (liaison at the intercept centres, 1989-90)
notes: Every number here is a game value ordered by those sources, not a measurement: the tiers' delays and error rates (osipov_2013 says only that a weak telegraphist mis-wrote words and a doubt was checked by telephone), the liaison's five minutes (anchored to the relay of nsa_purple_dragon_1993 pp. 60-61), the posts' linguists (the forward posts keep one language each; the centre has all). The liaison's date is open: it is documented only for 1989-90 (docs/air_battle/09 section 1.7), so for the 1985 war the fast road is a design choice and this file says so.

tiers.notes: The form's writing time by the linguist's tier (20-120 s: docs/air_battle/09 section 4.3); the chance that one digit in the call is written wrong, that a word is dropped, and that the doubt is checked by telephone up the chain before it goes on.

fast_road.notes: liaison_s: the liaison passes a call that names a time and a place to the division's air defence command post in about five minutes (comms-03, nsa_purple_dragon_1993 pp. 60-61). doubt_check_s: a doubtful call is checked by telephone first, as at Torgau. relay_untranslated_s: a post with no linguist for the language passes the call untranslated to a post that has one. area_m: a call naming a place this near the battery (or an object it covers) is precedence 2, else 1. names_battery_m: a written square this near the battery is the battery's square. habit_after: a codeword heard this many times after attacks is a learned habit (strike complete). daily_summary_hour: the air section's day summary is written at this local hour.

posts.notes: The company's centre has every language the theatre's airmen speak; it reads what the forward posts could not.

enemy_listeners.notes: section 6 of docs/air_battle/09: where the enemy's receivers stand, so that our nets are heard by link margin and not all at once. Positions are the theatre's east and north in km; heights and sensitivities are game values (no tier 1-4 source gives a 1985 set).

warsaw_pact.notes: A front's radio and radar intercept regiment behind its line (the north-eastern border, about 20 km back): VHF about 40 km, HF ground wave about 80 km (fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 15-2). Placed behind the line in roadmap S6 (B9 had it inside our country).
The Il-20M's orbit behind the line (docs/air_war/11_SUPPORT.md; fm_100_2_1_1984 p. 15-2: intercept ranges greatly extended when airborne). Place, height and set game values.

nato.notes: NATO's ground intercept of Pact voice in Europe was not found in the research (comms_emcon.md section 7): a game value, behind the western border (placed there in roadmap S6).
The RC-135's orbit behind the line (docs/air_war/11_SUPPORT.md). Place, height and set game values.

rebels.notes: A few posts with native speakers near their home ground (comms-25): game values.
